title: What Changes on the Real Robot: Delay, a Slow Actuator and Friction in the Loop, the Delay a Joint Can Stand, and Gains Chosen Against a Spread of Robots

questions.question: Which controller failed on the real joint?
options: The gentle one, which was too slow to catch the step
Both, once the delay was added
Neither: the difference was within the 2 percent band
The stiff one that looked quickest in the simulator
questions.explanation: The stiff gains were quicker in the simulator and rang without settling once the delay and lag were added. The gentle ones still settled.

questions.question: The stiff gains with 20 ms of delay and a 10 ms lag:
options: Settled in 0.24 s with 0.2 percent of overshoot, as before
Settled, but in 0.53 s
Hit the torque limit and stopped short of the target
Overshot 23.5 percent and did not settle
questions.explanation: Delay is phase lag at the frequency where the loop crosses, and a quick loop crosses high, where the same delay is more lag.

questions.question: The largest delay the stiff gains could stand was:
options: 19 ms
43 ms
20 ms, the delay of the test
10 ms, the lag of the motor
questions.explanation: 19 ms, which is why 20 ms was enough to break it. The gentle gains stood 43 ms, more than twice the margin.

questions.question: Over 100 random robots the gentle gains settled on:
options: 97 percent
46 percent
All of them
About half, the same as the stiff gains
questions.explanation: With the inertia, delay and lag drawn at random the gentle gains settled on 97 of 100 and the stiff ones on 46.

questions.question: How does the sim-to-real gap shrink?
options: By making the simulator's time step smaller
By measuring the real robot's delay and lag and putting them into the simulation and the margin
By raising the gains until the real joint is as quick as the simulated one
By adding random noise to the simulated sensor
questions.explanation: The gap here is things the simulator left out. Measure them on the robot, put them in, and choose gains with a margin over what was measured.

questions.question: What is the last word on a controller?
options: The simulator, once the delay and lag are in it
The margin in delay
The robot
The success rate over the random robots
questions.explanation: Each of those is evidence, and each rests on a model. A step test on the real joint is one test too, but it is of the thing itself.
